# @jocoding-ax-partners/design-system

> CSS-only design system built on HeroUI v3. This package has NO component exports.
> Every component comes from `@heroui/react`. This package ships one stylesheet:
> style overrides for HeroUI components, plus a set of design tokens.
>
> This file documents ONLY what this package adds on top of HeroUI. It is not a HeroUI
> reference: it names a HeroUI prop or variant only where one is needed to describe an
> override. Component APIs, prop tables and examples are deliberately absent — they
> belong to HeroUI and go stale on its releases. See "Finding component APIs" below.

## Install

```bash
npm install @jocoding-ax-partners/design-system @heroui/react@^3 @heroui/styles@^3 tailwindcss@^4
```

## Setup

Add one line to your Tailwind CSS entry file:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@jocoding-ax-partners/design-system/styles";
```

Do not import `@heroui/styles` separately — `@jocoding-ax-partners/design-system/styles` imports it as
its own first line, so HeroUI's sheet always lands ahead of these overrides. It stays
a peer dependency and must still be installed.

Place this import after `tailwindcss` and after any other stylesheet it should
override.

No `@source` directive is needed for HeroUI — its classes resolve against the
precompiled `@heroui/styles` sheet, not files Tailwind has to scan.

Everything else is upstream setup, not this package's:

- Tailwind v4 for your framework — https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation
- HeroUI install and requirements — https://v3.heroui.com/docs/react/getting-started/quick-start
- Providers, app-root wiring (e.g. `Toast.Provider`) — see the component's page under
  https://v3.heroui.com/docs/react/components/

## The one rule

```tsx
import { Button, Input, Modal } from "@heroui/react"; // correct
import { Button } from "@jocoding-ax-partners/design-system"; // does not exist — no JS is published
```

## Finding component APIs

For any HeroUI component — props, variants, sizes, compound structure, examples —
consult these in order:

1. The `heroui-react` MCP server (`list_components`, `get_component_docs`). Richest
   source — anatomy, props and examples in one call. If this project has no MCP
   server configured, adding it is recommended: the npm package is
   `@heroui/react-mcp`, and per-editor setup is at
   https://v3.heroui.com/docs/react/getting-started/mcp-server
2. `https://v3.heroui.com/docs/react/components/<name>`. To work out which component
   to reach for, or its exact kebab-case `<name>`, https://v3.heroui.com/react/llms.txt
   is a 50 KB index of every component with a one-line description. Do not fetch
   HeroUI's `llms-full.txt` or `llms-components.txt` — they are multi-megabyte.
3. `node_modules/@heroui/react/dist/components/<name>/<name>.d.ts`

Sources 1 and 2 describe the current v3 docs, which may be ahead of the version
installed here. Source 3 IS the installed version. When they disagree, 3 wins.

## Before nesting anything in a Trigger

Some HeroUI Triggers render their own `<button>`, others render `<div role="button">`,
and this has flipped between minor versions. Putting a `<Button>` inside the former
produces invalid nested-button HTML. Check the actual element before nesting:

```
node_modules/@heroui/react/dist/components/<name>/<name>.js
```

Collection children (`ListBox.Item`, `Dropdown.Item`, `Tabs.Tab`, `Tag`, …) read from
React Aria context rather than props. Rendering one outside its collection parent
throws at runtime rather than degrading.

## Extensions

The only authoring API this package adds. HeroUI's prop types cannot be extended, so
these ride on `data-*` attributes instead of props.

### Button — `data-color`

Applies to `variant="outline"` and `variant="ghost"` only.

```tsx
<Button variant="outline" data-color="danger">Delete</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" data-color="info">Details</Button>
```

Values: `accent` | `danger` | `success` | `warning` | `info`

### ToggleButton — `data-color`

Applies to `variant="default"` and `variant="ghost"`. Tints the **selected** state
only; the unselected state is unchanged.

```tsx
<ToggleButton data-color="success">Publish</ToggleButton>
```

Values: `accent` | `danger` | `success` | `warning` | `info`
`accent` is the base color, so the attribute is only needed for the other four.

### Chip — `data-color`

Adds the one color HeroUI's `color` prop does not have.

```tsx
<Chip data-color="info"><Chip.Label>Info</Chip.Label></Chip>
```

Values: `info`

May be combined with HeroUI's `color` prop — `data-color` wins by specificity, not
by import order.

### Checkbox.Control, Radio.Control — `data-size`, `data-rounded`

```tsx
<Checkbox.Control data-size="md" />          {/* larger control */}
<Radio.Control data-size="md" />
<Checkbox.Control data-rounded="true" />     {/* circular instead of square */}
<Checkbox.Control data-size="md" data-rounded="true" />
```

`data-size`: `md` — omit for the default, smaller size. Both controls.
`data-rounded`: `"true"` — Checkbox.Control only.

## Behavior overrides

Places where a HeroUI component renders differently here without a new authoring API.

### ListBox.ItemIndicator — selection is a background, not a check mark

Applies inside Select, ComboBox, Autocomplete and standalone ListBox.

The indicator element is hidden. A selected item is marked by an `accent-soft`
background instead — `accent-soft-hover` while hovered.

```tsx
<ListBox.Item id="florida" textValue="Florida">
  Florida
  <ListBox.ItemIndicator /> {/* opts this item into the accent background */}
</ListBox.Item>
```

The indicator is still what switches the styling on, so an item rendered without one
keeps HeroUI's own appearance, where selection is not marked at all. Custom content
passed to `ListBox.ItemIndicator` is hidden along with the default check mark.

## Tokens

Utilities this package registers. Names are listed so you know they exist; **read the
exact values from** `node_modules/@jocoding-ax-partners/design-system/dist/styles/index.css` rather than
assuming them.

Prefer these over hardcoded equivalents — `rounded-button-md` not `rounded-[10px]`,
`h-button-lg` not `h-12`, `text-heading-03` not `text-2xl`.

```
colors     accent-50 … accent-950        (bg-accent-600, text-accent-100, …)
           gray-850                      (a step Tailwind does not ship)
           info, info-hover, info-soft, info-soft-hover,
           info-foreground, info-soft-foreground

rounded-   button-xs, button-sm, button-md, button-lg
           input, list-box, list-box-item, toast, dialog, card
           calendar-cell, calendar-nav-button, calendar-range-edge
           lg-plus, 2xl-plus

spacing    button-sm, button-md, button-lg, input, list-box-item, field
           (registered as spacing, so h-button-lg, size-input, gap-field,
           p-field … all resolve)

text-      display-01 … display-04
           heading-01 … heading-05
           body-01 … body-03
           caption-01, caption-02
           (each carries its own line-height and letter-spacing)

variant    light:                        (the counterpart to HeroUI's dark:)
```

Parts of HeroUI's own palette are also re-valued without adding a utility name: the
gray scale (`gray-500`–`gray-950`, shifted to neutral oklch), the semantic brand
colors, and a number of surface, border, field and soft-foreground roles — some in
light mode only, some in dark only. Keep using HeroUI's utility names for these; only
the values differ. Which roles are overridden, and in which mode, is not enumerated
here — read the shipped stylesheet rather than assuming.
